payload.claim: The refused-branch commit message unconditionally states 'It was re-verified and reviewed before the refusal,' but `reverify()` is only called after the credential-in-patch, credential-in-subjects, patch-apply-conflict and `ParentGone` refusals return (all of those `return`/early-exit before line 835's `reverify` call). For those four of the seven refusal shapes, re-verification never ran, so the pushed commit falsely claims it did. The spec's own note ('A refused-branch commit says PACKAGE refused it and why, and that REVIEW ran') only promises a claim about REVIEW, not re-verification, so this oversells what happened on every early refusal path. No gate catches this because it is a string asserted about control flow that already finished, not a value any test compares against which refusal path produced it.
